questions.q: What does an upsert operation do that a plain update does not?
options: It deletes any record that doesn't match the file
It inserts a new record when no match is found, instead of failing
It skips validation rules for faster loading
It only works on the Account object
questions.explain: Update fails when no matching record exists. Upsert inserts a new record in that case instead, which is why it's safe to re-run.

questions.q: Why does upsert typically match on a custom External ID field instead of the Salesforce record Id?
options: External ID fields are faster to index than the Id field
Salesforce Id values are not unique within an object
Using the Salesforce Id for matching is deprecated and no longer supported
The source system usually doesn't know the Salesforce Id, but it does have its own identifier you can map
questions.explain: A source CSV generally has no idea what Salesforce Id a record will get. An External ID field lets you match using an identifier the source system already provides.

questions.q: In the Data Loader sequence, what's the most common reason the matching-field dropdown doesn't show the field you expected at step 5?
options: The field isn't marked as an External ID in its field definition
The CSV file has too many columns
Data Loader only supports matching on standard fields
The object needs to be refreshed in Setup first
questions.explain: That dropdown only lists fields marked External ID on the object. If the field isn't configured that way, it won't appear, regardless of the CSV.

questions.q: Why should you open the error file even when the job summary reports a high success rate, like 39 of 40 rows?
options: The error file is required to close out the Data Loader session
Error files overwrite the success file if left unopened
That remaining row represents real data that failed to load, and the error message says why
Salesforce automatically retries failed rows without needing review
questions.explain: A high percentage still leaves real, unsaved data behind. The error file's Error column tells you exactly what to fix before re-running just that row.

questions.q: In the lab scenario, after editing two rows' email addresses and re-running the same upsert file, what should the success file show for those two rows?
options: Created = true, since editing the email creates a new record
Created = false, since they matched existing records by External ID and were updated
An error, since the same External ID can't be submitted twice
Nothing — Data Loader skips rows that were already loaded once
questions.explain: The External ID still matches an existing Contact, so upsert updates that record (Created = false) instead of inserting a duplicate.
